_comment: SHARED CALENDAR-EVENT FIXTURES — read by BOTH implementations.
There are two parsers for PVE/systemd calendar events in this product:
Nimbus\Backups\CalendarSchedule (PHP, derives backup_expectations) and
the agent's Go evaluator (decides when a managed job actually fires).
They must agree, and dev rule 25 says the way to establish that is a
SHARED FIXTURE SET rather than two independently written suites — two
suites written from the same head prove that the head was consistent,
not that the implementations are.
PROVENANCE: every date below was worked out from a calendar, by hand,
not produced by running either parser. A fixture generated from one
implementation would make the other's test a check that it matches a
particular bug.
This file is authoritative in NimbusControl. The agent vendors a byte
identical copy at controlplane/testdata/calendar-fixtures.json, and each
repository asserts its own copy hashes to the value in `sha256` below.
That catches an accidental one-sided edit, which is the realistic
failure; it cannot catch a deliberate simultaneous edit to both, and it
is not pretending to.
2026-08-05 is a Wednesday. 2026-03-08 is US spring-forward.
TIMES ARE LOCAL WALL CLOCK in the fixture's timezone. Occurrences are
written as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' with a separate 'utc' field where the
distinction matters, because the whole point of the timezone tier is
that these two are not the same instant.

next_occurrences.why: the canonical business-hours schedule; the weekend gap is the case an average-based derivation gets wrong
sub-daily repetition; Saturday and Sunday are ordinary days here
weekly — two occurrences is one gap, which is why the derivation needs three
monthly; months have different lengths and the derivation must take the longest
half-hourly stepping from a non-zero minute
a WRAPPING weekday range covers sun, mon, tue only — not the five days between
asked at exactly the scheduled instant, 'next' means tomorrow — strictly after, not at-or-after
day 30 has no February; the month is SKIPPED, never clamped to the 28th
the same expression is 02:00 LOCAL in any zone; the instant differs, the expression does not
a DST-nonexistent wall time normalizes FORWARD rather than vanishing — skipping it would make one daily backup a 48h gap twice a year

largest_gap_seconds.why: THE case this whole derivation exists for: the average is 33.6h, the real Friday-to-Monday gap is 72h, and deriving from the average alerts every Monday on every business-hours schedule in the fleet
weekly — the window must EXTEND past 14 days to see a second and third occurrence
monthly derives the LONGEST month, not the first one it happens to see
mon/wed/fri: the Friday-to-Monday gap is 3 days, not the 2-day midweek one
a daily schedule stays 24h across a DST transition, because the nonexistent wall time normalized forward instead of being skipped
an expression that can never fire again has NO interval; inventing one marks the job overdue forever a fixed distance from now
February 30th never matches; the scan must terminate and report no interval
